Release the screwdriver so the rod springs out, then fit the cap bolt with its gasket at 6 N·m (4.4 lb-ft).
steps.title: Fit the cam chain tensioner

steps.instruction: Turn the crankshaft counterclockwise several full turns by hand; it must turn without any hard stop. Bring it back to TDC and check that the rotor mark and both cam sprocket marks line up again. If they do not, remove the tensioner and caps and correct the chain.
steps.title: Turn the engine and recheck timing
verification: All timing marks align at TDC

branches.condition: Intake clearances are within 0.12–0.19 mm and exhaust clearances within 0.17–0.24 mm.
branches.label: All clearances in spec

steps.instruction: With the engine cold and at TDC, measure all four valve clearances with feeler gauges. Spec: 0.12–0.19 mm intake, 0.17–0.24 mm exhaust. Write each one down.
steps.title: Measure the valve clearance

steps.instruction: For each valve that is out, note the number on its pad (the pad thickness in hundredths of a millimetre). New pad thickness equals old pad thickness plus the measured clearance minus a target clearance in the middle of the spec. Pads come from 1.20 mm to 2.40 mm in 0.05 mm steps; pick the one that brings the clearance inside spec. Remove the cams (tensioner first), swap the pads with numbers facing up, refit the cams on timing exactly as before with the caps at 10 N·m (7.4 lb-ft) and the tensioner reset, then measure all four clearances again.
steps.title: Change pads to correct the clearance

steps.instruction: Remove the rag from the chain tunnel. Fit the top timing chain guide. Coat the new head cover gasket with a thin film of Yamaha bond No. 1215, fit it with a new spark plug hole gasket, set the cover on and tighten the cover bolts to 10 N·m (7.4 lb-ft).
steps.title: Refit the head cover

steps.instruction: Refit the timing mark accessing screw at 6 N·m (4.4 lb-ft) and the crankshaft end accessing screw at 10 N·m (7.4 lb-ft), each with a lightly greased O-ring. Gap a new or checked spark plug to 0.6–0.7 mm and fit it at 13 N·m (9.6 lb-ft). Refit the breather hose.
steps.title: Refit the access screws and spark plug
verification: Spark plug gapped and at 13 N·m (9.6 lb-ft)

steps.instruction: Record the final clearances and the parts you replaced. Refit the engine or the removed parts using the engine refit guide, then follow the first-start guide; a new piston, rings, valves or cams need the half-throttle break-in.
steps.title: Hand over to refit and first start

title: Top end: tear down, measure and rebuild the head, valves, cylinder and piston

completeness: Strips the cylinder head cover, camshafts, cylinder head, valves, cylinder and piston, measures every wear point against its limit, renews what is worn (valves, guides, springs, rings, piston, pin), reassembles with correct cam timing and head bolt procedure, and sets the valve clearances; the crankcase stays closed.
critical_stop_conditions: Cylinder bore over 77.060 mm or vertical scoring: replace the cylinder, piston and rings as a set.
Head warpage over 0.05 mm that will not lap out flat: replace the head.
Valve seat pitted or worn, or seat contact width over its limit: replace the cylinder head.
Cam lobe below its limit (32.130 mm intake, 33.460 mm exhaust) or blue/pitted: replace the camshaft.
Timing marks will not line up after assembly: stop, do not run the engine; incorrect timing will bend valves.
Crankshaft turned while the cams are out of mesh: recheck timing before going on.
Anything dropped into the crankcase (pin clip, pad, cotter): stop and retrieve it.
entry_state: Engine on the bench (see the engine removal guide), or in the frame with the seat, side covers, shrouds, fuel tank, exhaust, throttle body, radiator hoses, coolant temperature coupler and upper engine brackets removed; oil and coolant drained.
excluded: Crankcase, crankshaft or gearbox work (see the bottom end guide)
Valve seat cutting (a worn or pitted seat means a new cylinder head)
Cylinder reboring or replating
exit_state: Top end assembled, cam timing checked, valve clearances in specification and recorded, head cover and spark plug fitted; ready for the engine refit and first-start guides.
prerequisites: Engine and work area clean; a clean tray with eight labeled spots for the valves, lifters and pads.
Oil and coolant drained.

required_parts.name: Cylinder head gasket, cylinder base gasket, head cover gasket and spark plug hole gasket
required_parts.purpose: Always new

required_parts.name: Valve stem seals
required_parts.purpose: Always new when a valve comes out

required_parts.name: Piston pin clips
required_parts.purpose: Always new

required_parts.name: Valves, guides, springs, piston, rings, pin
required_parts.purpose: Only where they measure out of limit

required_parts.name: Valve adjusting pads
required_parts.purpose: As needed to set the clearance

required_tools.name: Valve spring compressor with a 22 mm attachment
Valve guide remover, installer and reamer for 5 mm (intake) and 4.5 mm (exhaust) guides
Micrometers (outside) and a cylinder bore gauge

steps.instruction: Wash the outside of the engine and blow it dry so no dirt falls into the head. Set up a tray marked intake left/right and exhaust left/right for the lifters, pads and valve parts.
steps.title: Clean and lay out

steps.instruction: Pull off the cylinder head breather hose, remove the spark plug, undo the head cover bolts and lift the cover off. Take out the top timing chain guide and the cover gaskets.
steps.title: Remove the head cover

steps.instruction: Remove the timing mark accessing screw and the crankshaft end accessing screw from the left case cover. Turn the crankshaft counterclockwise with a wrench until the TDC mark on the generator rotor lines up with the mark on the case cover and the marks on both cam sprockets line up with the top faces of the cam caps. If the sprocket marks point the wrong way, turn one more full turn.
steps.title: Set the engine at top dead center
verification: Both cam sprocket marks level with the cap faces

steps.instruction: With the engine cold and at TDC, slide feeler gauges between each cam lobe and its lifter and note the clearance for all four valves. Spec is 0.12–0.19 mm intake and 0.17–0.24 mm exhaust. A clearance that has closed up a lot points to a worn valve or seat.
steps.title: Measure the valve clearance before teardown

steps.instruction: Remove the tensioner cap bolt, then the two tensioner bolts, and pull the tensioner and its gaskets out.
steps.title: Remove the cam chain tensioner

steps.instruction: Loosen the cam cap bolts a little at a time in a criss-cross pattern, working from the outside bolts in, so the caps come off evenly. Remove the caps and dowels. Lift out the two clips under the caps carefully so they cannot drop into the engine.
steps.title: Remove the cam caps
verification: No parts lost into the engine

steps.instruction: Lift out the exhaust camshaft and then the intake camshaft, slipping the chain off the sprockets. Tie the timing chain up with wire so it cannot fall into the crankcase. Stuff a clean rag into the chain tunnel.
steps.title: Lift out the camshafts

steps.instruction: Loosen the head fasteners in the reverse of the tightening order: the M6 nuts first, then the large head bolts in a criss-cross pattern, half a turn at a time until all are loose. Lift the head off while feeding the timing chain through, then remove the intake-side chain guide, the head gasket and the dowels.
steps.title: Remove the cylinder head

steps.instruction: Remove the cylinder bolt, then lift the cylinder straight up off the piston, guiding the timing chain and exhaust-side guide through. Remove the base gasket and dowels, and stuff a clean rag around the connecting rod to close the crankcase.
steps.title: Remove the cylinder

steps.instruction: With the rag in place, remove one piston pin clip. Clean any burr from the clip groove, then push the pin out by hand; use a pin puller if it is tight, never a hammer. Lift the piston off and remove the rings by spreading each one at its gap with your thumbs.
steps.title: Remove the piston

steps.instruction: Scrape carbon from the combustion chamber with a rounded scraper, keeping clear of the spark plug threads, and clear any scale from the coolant passages. Lay a straightedge across the gasket face in several directions and check warpage with a feeler gauge: the limit is 0.05 mm. If it is over, lap the face flat on 400–600 grit wet paper on a surface plate in a figure-eight, turning the head often, and measure again.
steps.title: Clean the head and check warpage
verification: Warpage at or under 0.05 mm, recorded

steps.instruction: Look at each lobe for blue heat marks, pitting or scratches. Measure each lobe height with a micrometer: intake limit 32.130 mm, exhaust limit 33.460 mm. A lobe under its limit means a new camshaft.
steps.title: Measure the camshafts

steps.instruction: Lay the cams in the head, put a strip of Plastigauge across each journal, fit the dowels and caps and torque the cap bolts to 10 N·m (7.4 lb-ft) in a criss-cross from the inner caps out. Do not turn the cams. Remove the caps and read the flattened strip: clearance must be 0.028–0.062 mm. If it is over, measure the cam journal diameter (spec 21.959–21.972 mm): a journal under size means a new camshaft; if the journal is in spec, the head and caps must be replaced as a set.
steps.title: Check the cam journal clearance
verification: Clearance read and recorded on every journal

steps.instruction: Check the chain for stiff links or damage and the cam sprockets for more than a quarter-tooth of wear (replace cams and chain together if so). Check the tensioner body for cracks; wind its rod fully in with a thin screwdriver while pressing it lightly, then release and make sure the rod comes out smoothly. Check the decompressor cam moves freely and its pin stands proud of the exhaust camshaft.
steps.title: Check the timing chain, sprockets and tensioner
verification: Chain, sprockets, tensioner and decompressor checked

steps.instruction: Before stripping the head, turn it over and pour solvent into the intake and exhaust ports. Watch the valve seats from the combustion chamber side: any seep means a valve, seat or seat width needs attention.
steps.title: Leak-test the valves
verification: Leak test done and result noted

steps.instruction: Lift out each valve lifter and its adjusting pad with a 14 mm valve lapping stick and put them in their labeled spots. Keep a rag in the chain tunnel so no pad falls into the engine.
steps.title: Remove the lifters and pads
verification: Lifters and pads labeled by position

steps.instruction: Compress each valve spring with the spring compressor, lift out the two cotters, release the spring and remove the retainer, spring, valve, stem seal and spring seat. Keep every part with its valve position.
steps.title: Remove the valves

steps.instruction: Measure each valve stem and guide bore and work out the stem-to-guide clearance (guide bore minus stem diameter). Limits are 0.080 mm intake and 0.100 mm exhaust. Check each stem for runout in V-blocks (limit 0.020 mm), the faces for pitting and the stem tips for mushrooming; any of these means a new valve, and a new valve always gets a new guide.
steps.title: Measure valves and guides

steps.instruction: Clean carbon off each valve face and seat. Paint blue layout fluid on the valve face, drop the valve in, press it onto the seat to leave an impression and measure the width of the contact band. Limits are 1.6 mm intake and 1.6 mm exhaust. A seat that is pitted, worn or over the limit means a new cylinder head.
steps.title: Check the valve seats

branches.condition: Every stem-to-guide clearance and runout is within limit, every seat width is within limit and no valve or guide needs replacing.
branches.label: Guides, valves and seats are within limits

steps.instruction: Measure each spring free length. Intake limit 34.94 mm, exhaust limit 33.82 mm. Replace any that are short. Check the lifters for scratches or damage; a damaged lifter bore means a new head.
steps.title: Measure the valve springs

steps.instruction: Drive the old guide out with the guide remover. Heating the head to about 100 °C (212 °F) in an oven makes removal and fitting easier and protects the bore. Drive the new guide in with the installer until it stands 11.8–12.2 mm (intake) or 11.2–11.6 mm (exhaust) above the head, then ream it to size with the guide reamer. A new guide always gets a new valve, and the seat must be lapped afterwards.
steps.title: Replace worn valve guides
verification: Guide height set: intake 11.8–12.2 mm, exhaust 11.2–11.6 mm

steps.instruction: Put coarse lapping compound on the valve face, oil the stem with molybdenum disulfide oil, and turn the valve back and forth with the lapping stick while tapping it on the seat. Keep compound out of the guide. Clean off, repeat with fine compound, clean everything off, then check the contact width again with layout fluid. These are titanium valves: a valve used for lapping must not be fitted. Lap with a spare valve, then fit a new one.
steps.title: Lap the seats

steps.instruction: Oil each valve stem and new stem seal with molybdenum disulfide oil. Fit the spring seat, a new stem seal, the valve, the spring with its wider-spaced coils facing up, and the retainer. Compress the spring and fit both cotters, then tap the stem tip lightly with a soft hammer to seat them. Each valve goes back in its own position.
steps.title: Fit the valves

steps.instruction: Oil the pads and lifters with engine oil and fit them back in their original positions with the pad numbers facing up. Each lifter must turn smoothly with a finger.
steps.title: Fit the pads and lifters
verification: Pads and lifters in original positions

steps.instruction: Check the bore and piston skirt for vertical scoring. Measure the bore front-to-back and side-to-side at three heights; the largest reading is the bore size. Spec is 77.000–77.010 mm, wear limit 77.060 mm. Measure the piston diameter 4.0 mm up from the bottom of the skirt (spec 76.955–76.970 mm). Piston-to-cylinder clearance is bore minus piston diameter and must be 0.030–0.055 mm. Any reading out means a new cylinder with a new piston and rings as a set.
steps.title: Measure the cylinder and piston

steps.instruction: Clean the carbon out of the ring grooves. Measure each compression ring side clearance in its groove (limits: top ring 0.115 mm). Push each ring squarely into the bottom of the bore with the piston crown and measure its end gap (limits: top ring 0.50 mm); the oil ring expander cannot be measured, so replace the oil ring as a set if its rails gap too much. Check the piston pin for blueing or grooves and measure it: outside diameter limit 15.971 mm, piston pin bore limit 16.043 mm.
steps.title: Measure the rings and pin
verification: Ring side clearances and end gaps recorded

steps.instruction: Fit the oil ring expander, the lower rail and the upper rail, then the top ring, all with their maker marks facing up. Oil the rings and stagger the end gaps around the piston so none line up with another.
steps.title: Fit the rings

steps.instruction: Oil the pin and piston. Put the piston on the rod with its arrow mark pointing to the exhaust side, push the pin in and fit new pin clips with the rag still over the crankcase. Make sure each clip is fully in its groove and its ends are not at the cutout in the piston.
steps.title: Fit the piston
verification: New clips seated, ends away from the cutout

steps.instruction: Fit the dowels and a new base gasket. Oil the bore and piston, compress the rings with your fingers and slide the cylinder down over the piston while feeding the timing chain and exhaust-side guide through the chain tunnel. Fit the cylinder bolt at 10 N·m (7.4 lb-ft).
steps.title: Fit the cylinder

steps.instruction: Fit the intake-side chain guide and the dowels, lay a new head gasket on the right way up, and lower the head onto the cylinder while pulling the timing chain up through it.
steps.title: Fit the cylinder head

steps.instruction: Clean the bolt threads, washers and crankcase threads, then coat the bolt threads and seats and both faces of each washer with molybdenum disulfide grease. Fit the big head bolts and bring them up to 30 N·m (22 lb-ft) over two or three passes, following the head bolt sequence. Now work one bolt at a time in the tightening order: loosen that bolt only, regrease it, retighten it to 15 N·m (11 lb-ft), paint a line on its head and turn it a further 60°. Do not touch the next bolt until this one is done. When all are done, paint new lines and turn every bolt a further 60° in the tightening order.
steps.title: Tighten the head bolts by torque and angle
verification: Torque and both angle stages done in order

steps.instruction: Tighten the two M6 head nuts to 10 N·m (7.4 lb-ft).
steps.title: Tighten the small head fasteners

steps.instruction: Check the rotor TDC mark is still lined up. Coat the cam journals and lobes with molybdenum disulfide oil and the decompressor with engine oil. Lay in the exhaust cam and then the intake cam with the chain over both sprockets, keeping the chain tight on the exhaust side, so that the sprocket marks line up with the cap faces. Do not turn the crankshaft while doing this. Before fitting the cam caps, cover the openings in the head with a rag and put the two clips in their places. Fit the caps and dowels, oil the bolt threads, and bring the cap bolts up to 10 N·m (7.4 lb-ft) gradually, over two or three passes, following the cap bolt sequence.
steps.title: Fit the camshafts on timing
verification: Sprocket marks level with the caps

steps.instruction: Wind the tensioner rod fully in with a thin screwdriver while pressing it lightly, and hold it there. Fit a new gasket, the tensioner with its UP mark upward, and tighten the two bolts to 10 N·m (7.4 lb-ft). Release the screwdriver so the rod springs out, then fit the cap bolt with its gasket at 6 N·m (4.4 lb-ft).
steps.title: Fit the cam chain tensioner

steps.instruction: Turn the crankshaft counterclockwise several full turns by hand; it must turn without any hard stop. Bring it back to TDC and check that the rotor mark and both cam sprocket marks line up again. If they do not, remove the tensioner and caps and correct the chain.
steps.title: Turn the engine and recheck timing
verification: All timing marks align at TDC

branches.condition: Intake clearances are within 0.12–0.19 mm and exhaust clearances within 0.17–0.24 mm.
branches.label: All clearances in spec

steps.instruction: With the engine cold and at TDC, measure all four valve clearances with feeler gauges. Spec: 0.12–0.19 mm intake, 0.17–0.24 mm exhaust. Write each one down.
steps.title: Measure the valve clearance

steps.instruction: For each valve that is out, note the number on its pad (the pad thickness in hundredths of a millimetre). New pad thickness equals old pad thickness plus the measured clearance minus a target clearance in the middle of the spec. Pads come from 1.20 mm to 2.40 mm in 0.05 mm steps; pick the one that brings the clearance inside spec. Remove the cams (tensioner first), swap the pads with numbers facing up, refit the cams on timing exactly as before with the caps at 10 N·m (7.4 lb-ft) and the tensioner reset, then measure all four clearances again.
steps.title: Change pads to correct the clearance

steps.instruction: Remove the rag from the chain tunnel. Fit the top timing chain guide. Coat the new head cover gasket with a thin film of Yamaha bond No. 1215, fit it with a new spark plug hole gasket, set the cover on and tighten the cover bolts to 10 N·m (7.4 lb-ft).
steps.title: Refit the head cover

steps.instruction: Refit the timing mark accessing screw at 6 N·m (4.4 lb-ft) and the crankshaft end accessing screw at 10 N·m (7.4 lb-ft), each with a lightly greased O-ring. Gap a new or checked spark plug to 0.6–0.7 mm and fit it at 13 N·m (9.6 lb-ft). Refit the breather hose.
steps.title: Refit the access screws and spark plug
verification: Spark plug gapped and at 13 N·m (9.6 lb-ft)

steps.instruction: Record the final clearances and the parts you replaced. Refit the engine or the removed parts using the engine refit guide, then follow the first-start guide; a new piston, rings, valves or cams need the half-throttle break-in.
steps.title: Hand over to refit and first start

title: Top end: tear down, measure and rebuild the head, valves, cylinder and piston

completeness: Strips the generator, clutch, primary drive, balancer drive, starter clutch, oil pump and shift mechanism, splits the crankcases, removes the gearbox, balancer shaft and crankshaft, checks every wear limit, and rebuilds with new seals, gaskets and any worn parts back to a closed bottom end ready for the top end; crankshaft and connecting rod internal repair is not covered (the crank is replaced as an assembly).
critical_stop_conditions: Crankshaft runout over 0.030 mm or crank width outside 55.93–56.00 mm: replace the crankshaft assembly.
Main or drive axle runout over 0.08 mm/0.08 mm: replace the axle.
Crankcase cracked or a bearing bore loose: replace the crankcases.
Cases will not separate with light tapping: stop and look for a bolt you missed; never lever on the gasket faces.
Gearbox does not shift through every gear on the bench: open it again before fitting the top end.
Crankshaft will not turn freely after the cases are bolted: stop and find the cause.
entry_state: Engine out of the frame (engine removal guide) with the top end stripped to the crankcase: head, cylinder and piston removed (top end guide). Oil and coolant drained.
excluded: Connecting rod or crankshaft bearing replacement (crank assembly is replaced as a unit)
Gear-by-gear transmission rebuild beyond inspecting and replacing damaged gears
Water pump seal service
Starter motor overhaul
exit_state: Bottom end closed and torqued with crank, balancer, gearbox, oil pump, clutch, starter clutch and generator refitted; gearbox shifts through every gear; ready for the top end rebuild.
prerequisites: Engine on a clean bench with a parts tray and labeled bags.
Top end already removed.

required_parts.name: Crankcase sealant, left and right case cover gaskets, clutch cover gasket or O-ring
required_parts.purpose: Always new

required_parts.name: All oil seals removed or disturbed, and all crankcase bearings removed
required_parts.purpose: Always new; a removed bearing is never reused

required_parts.name: Clutch boss nut and its lock or conical washer, all lock washers and circlips removed
required_parts.purpose: Always new

required_parts.name: Clutch friction and steel plates, springs, crankshaft assembly, gears, shift forks
required_parts.purpose: Only where they measure out of limit

required_tools.name: Crankshaft installer set (pot, bolt, M12 adapter and spacer)
Dial gauge with V-blocks or centres
Feeler gauges and a surface plate
Bearing driver set and a press
Aluminum plate (to lock the balancer gears)

steps.instruction: Mount the engine on a stand or blocks with the left side accessible, lay out labeled bags, and keep a notebook for the order and direction of shims, washers and forks as they come off.
steps.title: Set up the bench

steps.instruction: Remove the shift pedal (check its punch mark), then the left crankcase cover bolts and the cover with its gasket and dowels. The stator stays in the cover.
steps.title: Remove the left case cover

steps.instruction: Hold the rotor with a rotor holder and remove the rotor nut and washer. Pull the rotor off the crank taper with the rotor puller and take out the Woodruff key.
steps.title: Remove the generator rotor

steps.instruction: Remove the clutch cover bolts and the cover with its gasket.
steps.title: Remove the clutch cover

steps.instruction: Undo the six clutch spring bolts evenly in a criss-cross, remove the springs and the pressure plate, then push rod 1 with its bearing, washer and circlip, the ball and push rod 2.
steps.title: Remove springs and pressure plate

steps.instruction: Slide the friction and steel plates off and lay them out in order. Note the two black-marked friction plates at the ends and the six colored ones in between.
steps.title: Remove the clutch plates in order

steps.instruction: Lift the staked rib of the boss nut. Lock the boss with a clutch holder and undo the nut with hand tools only (no impact wrench), then take off the nut and conical washer. Lift off the clutch boss, the thrust washer and the primary driven gear (clutch housing).
steps.title: Remove the clutch boss
verification: Boss nut and conical washer off
Boss, thrust washer and driven gear off

steps.instruction: Remove the oil filter cover and the oil filter element, then the right crankcase cover bolts and the cover with its gasket and dowels. Remove the push lever shaft.
steps.title: Remove the right case cover

steps.instruction: Hold the clutch housing (primary driven gear) side with a sheave holder and remove the starter clutch screws. Separate the starter clutch gear, starter clutch, side plate, the eight absorbers, primary driven gear, spacer, collar and damper assembly, noting which way each part faces.
steps.title: Strip the clutch housing and starter clutch

steps.instruction: Remove the oil pump assembly. Wedge a folded aluminum plate between the balancer drive and weight gear teeth and loosen the balancer nut, the primary drive gear nut and the balancer weight gear nut. Remove the conical washers, balancer weights, primary drive gear, collars and gears in order, and the relief valve, its spring and pin.
steps.title: Remove the oil pump, balancer and primary drive
verification: Balancer parts and relief valve off in order

steps.instruction: Pull the shift shaft out with its spring and collar. Remove the shift guide and shift lever assembly, the stopper lever with its spring, and finally the segment: turn it counterclockwise to its stop before loosening its bolt, and do not let anything knock the stopper lever.
steps.title: Remove the shift mechanism
verification: Shift shaft, guide, stopper lever and segment off

steps.instruction: Remove the timing chain guide stopper plate, the exhaust-side chain guide and the timing chain.
steps.title: Remove the timing chain and guide

steps.instruction: With the left case facing down, loosen every crankcase bolt a quarter turn at a time in a criss-cross until all are loose, then remove them and note their lengths. Lever only at the splitting slot with a screwdriver tip and tap the reinforced bosses with a soft hammer to lift the right case off level. The crankshaft and gearbox stay in the left case. If it will not part, look for a bolt you missed.
steps.title: Split the crankcases
verification: Bolts out and sorted by length

steps.instruction: Pull the long and short shift fork guide bars, the shift cam and the three forks, noting which gear each fork sits in and which way it faces. Then lift both gearbox shafts out as one unit (a light tap on the drive axle with a soft hammer helps), followed by the collar.
steps.title: Remove the gearbox

steps.instruction: Turn the balancer shaft so its flat faces the crank, then lift it out. Press the crankshaft out of the left case with the crankcase separating tool.
steps.title: Remove the balancer shaft and crankshaft

steps.instruction: Support the crank on V-blocks or centres and turn it slowly under a dial gauge on the main journals: runout limit 0.030 mm. Measure the crank assembly width across the flywheels: 55.93–56.00 mm. Check the cam chain sprocket on the crank for damage and blow the oil passage clear.
steps.title: Measure the crankshaft

branches.condition: Every crankcase bearing turns smoothly with no play or pitting and no oil seal needs changing apart from the ones always renewed.
branches.label: All case bearings are good

steps.instruction: Wash both cases in mild solvent, remove all old gasket and sealant from the joint faces and blow out every oil passage. Check the cases for cracks. Turn each case bearing by finger: any roughness, play or pitting means replacement. Clean the oil strainer and check the timing chain and guides.
steps.title: Clean and inspect the cases and bearings

steps.instruction: Remove the bearing retainer plates. Measure how deep each old bearing sits, then press it out by its inner race (never reuse a removed bearing). Press the new bearing in square by its outer race to the same depth. Refit the retainer plates with medium threadlocker: plate bolts 12 N·m (8.9 lb-ft), crankshaft bearing plate screws 22 N·m (16 lb-ft).
steps.title: Replace worn case bearings

steps.instruction: Roll each fork guide bar on a flat surface (a bent bar is replaced, not straightened). Check each fork pawl and cam follower for wear or scoring, the shift cam grooves for wear, and that the forks slide freely on their bars. Measure axle runout: main axle limit 0.08 mm, drive axle limit 0.08 mm. Check every gear for blueing, pitting and rounded dogs, and that each gear moves freely on its shaft.
steps.title: Inspect the gearbox and shifting parts
verification: Forks, bars and shift cam good

steps.instruction: Measure each friction plate at four points: friction plates 1 spec 2.70–2.90 mm (limit 2.60 mm), friction plates 2 spec 2.72–2.88 mm (limit 2.62 mm). Check the steel plates for warpage on a surface plate (limit 0.10 mm). Measure each clutch spring free length (limit 41.80 mm; replace as a set). Roll push rod 2 for bend (limit 0.30 mm). Check the clutch housing dogs and boss splines for notching, the pressure plate for cracks, and the primary gears for wear or play.
steps.title: Measure the clutch

steps.instruction: Check the starter clutch rollers and the starter clutch gear contact face for wear. Fit the starter clutch gear onto the primary driven gear and hold the driven gear: turned clockwise it must lock, turned counterclockwise it must spin freely. Check the damper assembly and gears for burrs or wear.
steps.title: Check the starter clutch
verification: Starter clutch freewheels and locks correctly

steps.instruction: Check the pump housing, cover and drive shaft for cracks or wear. Measure the rotor clearances with feeler gauges: Inner-rotor-to-outer-rotor-tip clearance 0.00–0.15 mm; Limit 0.23 mm; Outer-rotor-to-oil-pump-housing clearance 0.13–0.18 mm; Limit 0.25 mm; Oil-pump-housing-to-inner-and-outer-rotor 0.06–0.11 mm; Limit 0.18 mm. Anything over its limit means a new pump.
steps.title: Measure the oil pump

steps.instruction: Grease the left case oil seal lip with lithium-soap grease and coat the crank journals with molybdenum disulfide grease. Using the crankshaft installer pot, bolt, M12 adapter and spacer, pull the crank into the left case bearing, keeping the rod held at the top of its stroke, until the crank seats against the bearing. Never hammer the crank in.
steps.title: Install the crankshaft

steps.instruction: Drop the balancer shaft in with its flat turned toward the crankshaft.
steps.title: Fit the balancer shaft

steps.instruction: Rebuild each shaft exactly as it came apart, with molybdenum disulfide oil on the gear bores and sliding gear faces, new circlips with their sharp edge away from the thrust washer and their ends on a spline crest, and a new greased O-ring on the drive axle. Fit the collar into the case oil seal with its slit toward the case. Fit the main axle and drive axle into the left case together. Oil the fork grooves and fit the forks: the left fork into the 5th wheel gear, the right fork into the 6th wheel gear, and the center fork into the 3rd/4th pinion gear. Fit the shift cam, then the long and short guide bars with their springs.
steps.title: Fit the gearbox

steps.instruction: Turn the shift cam by hand through every gear while turning the main axle; every gear must engage cleanly and the axles must spin freely in neutral.
steps.title: Check the shifting on the bench

steps.instruction: Press a new oil seal into the left case to an installed depth of 4.5–5.0 mm. Fit oil nozzle 1 to the right case (bolt 5 N·m (3.7 lb-ft), medium threadlocker). Fit the dowel pins, and spread a thin even bead of Yamaha bond No. 1215 on the left case joint face.
steps.title: Prepare the case halves
verification: Sealant even, not in oil passages

steps.instruction: Bring the rod up to the top of its stroke and lower the right case onto the left, tapping it down evenly with a soft hammer. Fit the bolts in their correct length positions and tighten them in a criss-cross in two stages to 12 N·m (8.9 lb-ft). Turn the crank and the main axle: both must turn freely.
steps.title: Close and torque the crankcases

steps.instruction: Fit the oil strainer (bolts 10 N·m (7.4 lb-ft)). Fit the timing chain, the exhaust-side chain guide and its stopper plate with medium threadlocker at 10 N·m (7.4 lb-ft).
steps.title: Fit the strainer, chain and guide
verification: Chain guide plate at 10 N·m (7.4 lb-ft)

steps.instruction: With the stopper lever pushed down, fit the segment so its projections sit in the slits of the shift cam, and tighten the segment bolt to 30 N·m (22 lb-ft) without jarring the stopper lever. Fit the stopper lever spring, collar and lever with threadlocker on its bolt at 10 N·m (7.4 lb-ft). Assemble the shift lever with its pawls, pins and springs (oiled), fit it with the shift guide and tighten the guide bolts with threadlocker to 10 N·m (7.4 lb-ft). Fit the shift shaft with its roller, spring and collar, oiled, and a new oil seal.
steps.title: Refit the shift mechanism

steps.instruction: Fit the relief valve spring, relief valve and pin before the primary drive gear and collar, and make sure the valve cannot fall out.
steps.title: Refit the relief valve

steps.instruction: Oil the drive shaft and rotors, fit the inner rotor with its dowel in the groove, the outer rotor and the cover (screw 2.0 N·m (1.5 lb-ft)). Fit the pump with threadlocker on its bolts at 5 N·m (3.7 lb-ft) and check it turns smoothly.
steps.title: Assemble and fit the oil pump

steps.instruction: Fit the collar and balancer weight gear with its lower spline lined up with the balancer shaft. Fit the balancer drive gear and collar with the punch marks of the two gears lined up and its lower spline lined up with the crank. Fit a new conical washer and the balancer weight gear nut at 50 N·m (37 lb-ft). Fit the primary drive gear, a new conical washer (convex side out) and the primary drive gear nut with threadlocker on the specified band of its thread at 105 N·m (77 lb-ft). Fit the balancer weight with its flat lined up with the shaft flat, a new conical washer and the balancer nut at 38 N·m (28 lb-ft). Keep the aluminum plate between the gears while torquing.
steps.title: Refit the balancer and primary drive
verification: Weight gear nut at 50 N·m (37 lb-ft)
Primary drive nut at 105 N·m (77 lb-ft)

steps.instruction: Rebuild the primary driven gear, absorbers and side plate with the 5XC-marked side of the absorbers toward the side plate and the B7B-marked side of the side plate toward the starter clutch, then fit the starter clutch with its arrow side toward the primary driven gear. Hold the housing with the sheave holder and fit the starter clutch screws with threadlocker at 12 N·m (8.9 lb-ft). Refit the damper assembly, collar and spacer.
steps.title: Rebuild the clutch housing and starter clutch
verification: Starter clutch screws at 12 N·m (8.9 lb-ft)

steps.instruction: Fit new dowels and gasket and the right crankcase cover, tightening the bolts in stages in a criss-cross to 10 N·m (7.4 lb-ft). Fit the push lever shaft with greased seal lips and oiled bearings.
steps.title: Refit the right case cover
verification: Right cover bolts at 10 N·m (7.4 lb-ft)

steps.instruction: Oil the primary driven gear bore and fit the primary driven gear, thrust washer and clutch boss and washer. Fit a new conical washer with its OUT mark facing away from the engine and a new boss nut with oiled thread and face; hold the boss with the clutch holder, torque the nut to 95 N·m (70 lb-ft) by hand (no impact wrench) and stake it into the main axle cutouts.
steps.title: Refit the clutch boss

steps.instruction: Oil every plate. Starting and ending with a friction plate, alternate friction and steel plates: one black-marked friction plate first, the six colored friction plates in the middle, and the second black-marked plate last.
steps.title: Refit the clutch plates
verification: Starts and ends with a black friction plate

steps.instruction: Fit the bearing, washer and a new circlip on push rod 1 and oil it. Fit push rod 2, the ball and push rod 1. Fit the pressure plate, lining its mark up with the punch mark on the clutch housing, then the six springs and bolts, tightened in stages in a criss-cross to 10 N·m (7.4 lb-ft).
steps.title: Refit the push rods, pressure plate and springs

steps.instruction: Fit a new clutch cover gasket and the cover, bolts in stages to 10 N·m (7.4 lb-ft). Fit a new oil filter element and cover with its O-ring (bolts 10 N·m (7.4 lb-ft)).
steps.title: Refit the clutch cover and oil filter

steps.instruction: Clean the crank taper and the rotor bore so they are dry. Fit the Woodruff key with its flat face parallel to the crank axis, slide the rotor on with its keyway over the key, fit the washer and nut, hold the rotor and torque the nut to 65 N·m (48 lb-ft).
steps.title: Refit the generator rotor
verification: Key flat parallel to the crank

steps.instruction: If the stator or crank position sensor was disturbed, refit them with threadlocker: stator screws 10 N·m (7.4 lb-ft), sensor bolts 10 N·m (7.4 lb-ft) and the lead holder (8 N·m (5.9 lb-ft), threadlocker), with sealant on the lead grommet.
steps.title: Check the stator and pickup in the cover
verification: Stator and sensor fasteners at spec

steps.instruction: Fit the dowels and a new gasket, then the left cover with its bolts in stages in a criss-cross to 10 N·m (7.4 lb-ft). Fit the shift pedal on its punch mark at 12 N·m (8.9 lb-ft).
steps.title: Refit the left case cover and shift pedal
verification: Left cover bolts at 10 N·m (7.4 lb-ft)

steps.instruction: Turn the crankshaft by hand through several turns (the piston is not fitted yet, so keep the rod clear of the case edge) and shift through every gear while turning the output shaft. Write down every part you replaced. Continue with the top end guide.
steps.title: Final bottom end check

steps.instruction: Hold the clutch housing (primary driven gear) side with a sheave holder and remove the starter clutch screws. steps.instruction: Pull the shift shaft out with its spring and collar. Remove the shift guide and shift lever assembly, the stopper lever with its spring, and finally the segment: turn it counterclockwise to its stop before loosening its bolt, and do not let anything knock the stopper lever.

verification: Shift shaft, guide, stopper lever and segment off

steps.instruction: With the left case facing down, loosen every crankcase bolt a quarter turn at a time in a criss-cross until all are loose, then remove them and note their lengths. Lever only at the splitting slot with a screwdriver tip and tap the reinforced bosses with a soft hammer to lift the right case off level. The crankshaft and gearbox stay in the left case. If it will not part, look for a bolt you missed.

verification: Bolts out and sorted by length

steps.instruction: Pull the long and short shift fork guide bars, the shift cam and the three forks, noting which gear each fork sits in and which way it faces. Then lift both gearbox shafts out as one unit (a light tap on the drive axle with a soft hammer helps), followed by the collar.

steps.instruction: Turn the balancer shaft so its flat faces the crank, then lift it out. Press the crankshaft out of the left case with the crankcase separating tool.

steps.instruction: Support the crank on V-blocks or centres and turn it slowly under a dial gauge on the main journals: runout limit 0.030 mm. Measure the crank assembly width across the flywheels: 55.93–56.00 mm. Check the cam chain sprocket on the crank for damage and blow the oil passage clear.

steps.instruction: Wash both cases in mild solvent, remove all old gasket and sealant from the joint faces and blow out every oil passage. Check the cases for cracks. steps.instruction: Remove the bearing retainer plates. Measure how deep each old bearing sits, then press it out by its inner race (never reuse a removed bearing). Press the new bearing in square by its outer race to the same depth. Refit the retainer plates with medium threadlocker: plate bolts 12 N·m (8.9 lb-ft), crankshaft bearing plate screws 22 N·m (16 lb-ft).

steps.instruction: Roll each fork guide bar on a flat surface (a bent bar is replaced, not straightened). Check each fork pawl and cam follower for wear or scoring, the shift cam grooves for wear, and that the forks slide freely on their bars. Measure axle runout: main axle limit 0.08 mm, drive axle limit 0.08 mm. Check every gear for blueing, pitting and rounded dogs, and that each gear moves freely on its shaft.

verification: Forks, bars and shift cam good

steps.instruction: Measure each friction plate at four points: friction plates 1 spec 2.70–2.90 mm (limit 2.60 mm), friction plates 2 spec 2.72–2.88 mm (limit 2.62 mm). Check the steel plates for warpage on a surface plate (limit 0.10 mm). Measure each clutch spring free length (limit 41.80 mm; replace as a set). Roll push rod 2 for bend (limit 0.30 mm). Check the clutch housing dogs and boss splines for notching, the pressure plate for cracks, and the primary gears for wear or play.

steps.instruction: Check the starter clutch rollers and the starter clutch gear contact face for wear. Fit the starter clutch gear onto the primary driven gear and hold the driven gear: turned clockwise it must lock, turned counterclockwise it must spin freely. Check the damper assembly and gears for burrs or wear.

verification: Starter clutch freewheels and locks correctly

Never hammer the crank in.

steps.instruction: Drop the balancer shaft in with its flat turned toward the crankshaft.

Lever only at the splitting slot with a screwdriver tip and tap the reinforced bosses with a soft hammer to lift the right case off level. The crankshaft and gearbox stay in the left case. If it will not part, look for a bolt you missed.
steps.title: Split the crankcases
verification: Bolts out and sorted by length

steps.instruction: Pull the long and short shift fork guide bars, the shift cam and the three forks, noting which gear each fork sits in and which way it faces. Then lift both gearbox shafts out as one unit (a light tap on the drive axle with a soft hammer helps), followed by the collar.
steps.title: Remove the gearbox

steps.instruction: Turn the balancer shaft so its flat faces the crank, then lift it out. Press the crankshaft out of the left case with the crankcase separating tool.
steps.title: Remove the balancer shaft and crankshaft

steps.instruction: Support the crank on V-blocks or centres and turn it slowly under a dial gauge on the main journals: runout limit 0.030 mm. Measure the crank assembly width across the flywheels: 55.93–56.00 mm. Check the cam chain sprocket on the crank for damage and blow the oil passage clear.
steps.title: Measure the crankshaft

branches.condition: Every crankcase bearing turns smoothly with no play or pitting and no oil seal needs changing apart from the ones always renewed.
branches.label: All case bearings are good

steps.instruction: Wash both cases in mild solvent, remove all old gasket and sealant from the joint faces and blow out every oil passage. Check the cases for cracks. Turn each case bearing by finger: any roughness, play or pitting means replacement. Clean the oil strainer and check the timing chain and guides.
steps.title: Clean and inspect the cases and bearings

steps.instruction: Remove the bearing retainer plates. Measure how deep each old bearing sits, then press it out by its inner race (never reuse a removed bearing). Press the new bearing in square by its outer race to the same depth. Refit the retainer plates with medium threadlocker: plate bolts 12 N·m (8.9 lb-ft), crankshaft bearing plate screws 22 N·m (16 lb-ft).
steps.title: Replace worn case bearings

steps.instruction: Roll each fork guide bar on a flat surface (a bent bar is replaced, not straightened). Check each fork pawl and cam follower for wear or scoring, the shift cam grooves for wear, and that the forks slide freely on their bars. Measure axle runout: main axle limit 0.08 mm, drive axle limit 0.08 mm. Check every gear for blueing, pitting and rounded dogs, and that each gear moves freely on its shaft.
steps.title: Inspect the gearbox and shifting parts
verification: Forks, bars and shift cam good

steps.instruction: Measure each friction plate at four points: friction plates 1 spec 2.70–2.90 mm (limit 2.60 mm), friction plates 2 spec 2.72–2.88 mm (limit 2.62 mm). Check the steel plates for warpage on a surface plate (limit 0.10 mm). Measure each clutch spring free length (limit 42.27 mm; replace as a set). Roll push rod 2 for bend (limit 0.30 mm). Check the clutch housing dogs and boss splines for notching, the pressure plate for cracks, and the primary gears for wear or play.
steps.title: Measure the clutch

steps.instruction: Check the starter clutch rollers and the starter clutch gear contact face for wear. Fit the starter clutch gear onto the primary driven gear and hold the driven gear: turned clockwise it must lock, turned counterclockwise it must spin freely. Check the damper assembly and gears for burrs or wear.
steps.title: Check the starter clutch
verification: Starter clutch freewheels and locks correctly

steps.instruction: Check the pump housing, cover, rotors and drive shaft for cracks, scoring or wear. Assemble the rotors dry and turn the shaft; any roughness means a new pump assembly.
steps.title: Check the oil pump

steps.instruction: Grease the left case oil seal lip with lithium-soap grease and coat the crank journals with molybdenum disulfide grease. Using the crankshaft installer pot, bolt, M12 adapter and spacer, pull the crank into the left case bearing, keeping the rod held at the top of its stroke, until the crank seats against the bearing. Never hammer the crank in.
steps.title: Install the crankshaft

steps.instruction: Drop the balancer shaft in with its flat turned toward the crankshaft.
steps.title: Fit the balancer shaft

steps.instruction: Rebuild each shaft exactly as it came apart, with molybdenum disulfide oil on the gear bores and sliding gear faces, new circlips with their sharp edge away from the thrust washer and their ends on a spline crest, and a new greased O-ring on the drive axle. Fit the collar into the case oil seal with its slit toward the case. Fit the main axle and drive axle into the left case together. Oil the fork grooves and fit the forks: the left fork into the 5th wheel gear, the right fork into the 6th wheel gear, and the center fork into the 3rd/4th pinion gear. Fit the shift cam, then the long and short guide bars with their springs.
steps.title: Fit the gearbox

steps.instruction: Turn the shift cam by hand through every gear while turning the main axle; every gear must engage cleanly and the axles must spin freely in neutral.
steps.title: Check the shifting on the bench

steps.instruction: Press a new oil seal into the left case to an installed depth of 4.5–5.0 mm. Fit oil nozzle 1 to the right case (bolt 5 N·m (3.7 lb-ft), medium threadlocker). Fit the dowel pins, and spread a thin even bead of Yamaha bond No. 1215 on the left case joint face.
steps.title: Prepare the case halves
verification: Sealant even, not in oil passages

steps.instruction: Bring the rod up to the top of its stroke and lower the right case onto the left, tapping it down evenly with a soft hammer. Fit the bolts in their correct length positions and tighten them in a criss-cross in two stages to 12 N·m (8.9 lb-ft). Turn the crank and the main axle: both must turn freely.
steps.title: Close and torque the crankcases

steps.instruction: Fit the oil strainer (bolts 10 N·m (7.4 lb-ft)). Fit the timing chain, the exhaust-side chain guide and its stopper plate with medium threadlocker at 10 N·m (7.4 lb-ft).
steps.title: Fit the strainer, chain and guide
verification: Chain guide plate at 10 N·m (7.4 lb-ft)

steps.instruction: With the stopper lever pushed down, fit the segment so its projections sit in the slits of the shift cam, and tighten the segment bolt to 30 N·m (22 lb-ft) without jarring the stopper lever. Fit the stopper lever spring, collar and lever with threadlocker on its bolt at 10 N·m (7.4 lb-ft). Assemble the shift lever with its pawls, pins and springs (oiled), fit it with the shift guide and tighten the guide bolts with threadlocker to 10 N·m (7.4 lb-ft). Fit the shift shaft with its roller, spring and collar, oiled, and a new oil seal.
steps.title: Refit the shift mechanism

steps.instruction: Fit the relief valve spring, relief valve and pin before the primary drive gear and collar, and make sure the valve cannot fall out.
steps.title: Refit the relief valve

steps.instruction: Oil the drive shaft and rotors, fit the inner rotor with its dowel in the groove, the outer rotor and the cover (screw 6 N·m (4.4 lb-ft)). Fit the pump with threadlocker on its bolts at 5 N·m (3.7 lb-ft) and check it turns smoothly.
steps.title: Assemble and fit the oil pump

steps.instruction: Fit the collar and balancer weight gear with its lower spline lined up with the balancer shaft. Fit the balancer drive gear and collar with the punch marks of the two gears lined up and its lower spline lined up with the crank. Fit a new conical washer and the balancer weight gear nut at 50 N·m (37 lb-ft). Fit the primary drive gear, a new conical washer (convex side out) and the primary drive gear nut with threadlocker on the specified band of its thread at 105 N·m (77 lb-ft). Fit the balancer weight with its flat lined up with the shaft flat, a new conical washer and the balancer nut at 38 N·m (28 lb-ft). Keep the aluminum plate between the gears while torquing.
steps.title: Refit the balancer and primary drive
verification: Weight gear nut at 50 N·m (37 lb-ft)
Primary drive nut at 105 N·m (77 lb-ft)

steps.instruction: Rebuild the primary driven gear, absorbers and side plate with the 5XC-marked side of the absorbers toward the side plate and the B7B-marked side of the side plate toward the starter clutch, then fit the starter clutch with its arrow side toward the primary driven gear. Hold the housing with the sheave holder and fit the starter clutch screws with threadlocker at 12 N·m (8.9 lb-ft). Refit the damper assembly, collar and spacer.
steps.title: Rebuild the clutch housing and starter clutch
verification: Starter clutch screws at 12 N·m (8.9 lb-ft)

steps.instruction: Fit new dowels and gasket and the right crankcase cover, tightening the bolts in stages in a criss-cross to 10 N·m (7.4 lb-ft). Fit the push lever shaft with greased seal lips and oiled bearings.
steps.title: Refit the right case cover
verification: Right cover bolts at 10 N·m (7.4 lb-ft)

steps.instruction: Oil the primary driven gear bore and fit the primary driven gear, thrust washer and clutch boss and washer. Fit a new conical washer with its OUT mark facing away from the engine and a new boss nut with oiled thread and face; hold the boss with the clutch holder, torque the nut to 95 N·m (70 lb-ft) by hand (no impact wrench) and stake it into the main axle cutouts.
steps.title: Refit the clutch boss

steps.instruction: Oil every plate. Starting and ending with a friction plate, alternate friction and steel plates: one black-marked friction plate first, the six colored friction plates in the middle, and the second black-marked plate last.
steps.title: Refit the clutch plates
verification: Starts and ends with a black friction plate

steps.instruction: Fit the bearing, washer and a new circlip on push rod 1 and oil it. Fit push rod 2, the ball and push rod 1. Fit the pressure plate, lining its mark up with the punch mark on the clutch housing, then the six springs and bolts, tightened in stages in a criss-cross to 10 N·m (7.4 lb-ft).
steps.title: Refit the push rods, pressure plate and springs

steps.instruction: Fit a new clutch cover gasket and the cover, bolts in stages to 10 N·m (7.4 lb-ft). Fit a new oil filter element and cover with its O-ring (bolts 10 N·m (7.4 lb-ft)).
steps.title: Refit the clutch cover and oil filter

steps.instruction: Clean the crank taper and the rotor bore so they are dry. Fit the Woodruff key with its flat face parallel to the crank axis, slide the rotor on with its keyway over the key, fit the washer and nut, hold the rotor and torque the nut to 65 N·m (48 lb-ft).
steps.title: Refit the generator rotor
verification: Key flat parallel to the crank

steps.instruction: If the stator or crank position sensor was disturbed, refit them with threadlocker: stator screws 10 N·m (7.4 lb-ft), sensor bolts 10 N·m (7.4 lb-ft) and the lead holder (8 N·m (5.9 lb-ft), threadlocker), with sealant on the lead grommet.
steps.title: Check the stator and pickup in the cover
verification: Stator and sensor fasteners at spec

steps.instruction: Fit the dowels and a new gasket, then the left cover with its bolts in stages in a criss-cross to 10 N·m (7.4 lb-ft). Fit the shift pedal on its punch mark at 12 N·m (8.9 lb-ft).
steps.title: Refit the left case cover and shift pedal
verification: Left cover bolts at 10 N·m (7.4 lb-ft)

steps.instruction: Turn the crankshaft by hand through several turns (the piston is not fitted yet, so keep the rod clear of the case edge) and shift through every gear while turning the output shaft. Write down every part you replaced. Continue with the top end guide.
steps.title: Final bottom end check

title: Bottom end: split the cases and rebuild crank, gearbox, clutch, balancer and oil pump

completeness: Strips the generator, clutch, primary drive, balancer drive, starter clutch, oil pump and shift mechanism, splits the crankcases, removes the gearbox, balancer shaft and crankshaft, checks every wear limit, and rebuilds with new seals, gaskets and any worn parts back to a closed bottom end ready for the top end; crankshaft and connecting rod internal repair is not covered (the crank is replaced as an assembly).
critical_stop_conditions: Crankshaft runout over 0.030 mm or crank width outside 55.93–56.00 mm: replace the crankshaft assembly.
Main or drive axle runout over 0.08 mm/0.08 mm: replace the axle.
Crankcase cracked or a bearing bore loose: replace the crankcases.
Cases will not separate with light tapping: stop and look for a bolt you missed; never lever on the gasket faces.
Gearbox does not shift through every gear on the bench: open it again before fitting the top end.
Crankshaft will not turn freely after the cases are bolted: stop and find the cause.
entry_state: Engine out of the frame (engine removal guide) with the top end stripped to the crankcase: head, cylinder and piston removed (top end guide). Oil and coolant drained.
excluded: Connecting rod or crankshaft bearing replacement (crank assembly is replaced as a unit)
Gear-by-gear transmission rebuild beyond inspecting and replacing damaged gears
Water pump seal service
Starter motor overhaul
exit_state: Bottom end closed and torqued with crank, balancer, gearbox, oil pump, clutch, starter clutch and generator refitted; gearbox shifts through every gear; ready for the top end rebuild.
prerequisites: Engine on a clean bench with a parts tray and labeled bags.
Top end already removed.

steps.instruction: Mount the engine on a stand or blocks with the left side accessible, lay out labeled bags, and keep a notebook for the order and direction of shims, washers and forks as they come off.
steps.title: Set up the bench

steps.instruction: Remove the shift pedal (check its punch mark), then the left crankcase cover bolts and the cover with its gasket and dowels. The stator stays in the cover.
steps.title: Remove the left case cover

steps.instruction: Hold the rotor with a rotor holder and remove the rotor nut and washer. Pull the rotor off the crank taper with the rotor puller and take out the Woodruff key.
steps.title: Remove the generator rotor

steps.instruction: Remove the clutch cover bolts and the cover with its gasket.
steps.title: Remove the clutch cover

steps.instruction: Undo the six clutch spring bolts evenly in a criss-cross, remove the springs and the pressure plate, then push rod 1 with its bearing, washer and circlip, the ball and push rod 2.
steps.title: Remove springs and pressure plate

steps.instruction: Slide the friction and steel plates off and lay them out in order. Note the two black-marked friction plates at the ends and the six colored ones in between.
steps.title: Remove the clutch plates in order

steps.instruction: Lift the staked rib of the boss nut. Lock the boss with a clutch holder and undo the nut with hand tools only (no impact wrench), then take off the nut and conical washer. Lift off the clutch boss, the thrust washer and the primary driven gear (clutch housing).
steps.title: Remove the clutch boss
verification: Boss nut and conical washer off
Boss, thrust washer and driven gear off

steps.instruction: Remove the oil filter cover and the oil filter element, then the right crankcase cover bolts and the cover with its gasket and dowels. Remove the push lever shaft.
steps.title: Remove the right case cover

steps.instruction: Hold the clutch housing (primary driven gear) side with a sheave holder and remove the starter clutch screws. Separate the starter clutch gear, starter clutch, side plate, the eight absorbers, primary driven gear, spacer, collar and damper assembly, noting which way each part faces.
steps.title: Strip the clutch housing and starter clutch

steps.instruction: Remove the oil pump assembly. Wedge a folded aluminum plate between the balancer drive and weight gear teeth and loosen the balancer nut, the primary drive gear nut and the balancer weight gear nut. Remove the conical washers, balancer weights, primary drive gear, collars and gears in order, and the relief valve, its spring and pin.
steps.title: Remove the oil pump, balancer and primary drive
verification: Balancer parts and relief valve off in order

steps.instruction: Pull the shift shaft out with its spring and collar. Remove the shift guide and shift lever assembly, the stopper lever with its spring, and finally the segment: turn it counterclockwise to its stop before loosening its bolt, and do not let anything knock the stopper lever.
steps.title: Remove the shift mechanism
verification: Shift shaft, guide, stopper lever and segment off

steps.instruction: Remove the timing chain guide stopper plate, the exhaust-side chain guide and the timing chain.
steps.title: Remove the timing chain and guide

steps.instruction: With the left case facing down, loosen every crankcase bolt a quarter turn at a time in a criss-cross until all are loose, then remove them and note their lengths. Lever only at the splitting slot with a screwdriver tip and tap the reinforced bosses with a soft hammer to lift the right case off level. The crankshaft and gearbox stay in the left case. If it will not part, look for a bolt you missed.
steps.title: Split the crankcases
verification: Bolts out and sorted by length

steps.instruction: Pull the long and short shift fork guide bars, the shift drum and the three forks, noting which gear each fork sits in and which way it faces. Then lift both gearbox shafts out as one unit (a light tap on the drive axle with a soft hammer helps), followed by the collar.
steps.title: Remove the gearbox

steps.instruction: Turn the balancer shaft so its flat faces the crank, then lift it out. Press the crankshaft out of the left case with the crankcase separating tool.
steps.title: Remove the balancer shaft and crankshaft

steps.instruction: Support the crank on V-blocks or centres and turn it slowly under a dial gauge on the main journals: runout limit 0.030 mm. Measure the crank assembly width across the flywheels: 55.93–56.00 mm. Check the cam chain sprocket on the crank for damage and blow the oil passage clear.
steps.title: Measure the crankshaft

branches.condition: Every crankcase bearing turns smoothly with no play or pitting and no oil seal needs changing apart from the ones always renewed.
branches.label: All case bearings are good

steps.instruction: Wash both cases in mild solvent, remove all old gasket and sealant from the joint faces and blow out every oil passage. Check the cases for cracks. Turn each case bearing by finger: any roughness, play or pitting means replacement. Clean the oil strainer and check the timing chain and guides.
steps.title: Clean and inspect the cases and bearings

steps.instruction: Remove the bearing retainer plates. Measure how deep each old bearing sits, then press it out by its inner race (never reuse a removed bearing). Press the new bearing in square by its outer race to the same depth. Refit the retainer plates with medium threadlocker: plate bolts 12 N·m (8.9 lb-ft), crankshaft bearing plate screws 22 N·m (16 lb-ft).
steps.title: Replace worn case bearings

steps.instruction: Roll each fork guide bar on a flat surface (a bent bar is replaced, not straightened). Check each fork pawl and cam follower for wear or scoring, the shift drum grooves for wear, and that the forks slide freely on their bars. Measure axle runout: main axle limit 0.08 mm, drive axle limit 0.08 mm. Check every gear for blueing, pitting and rounded dogs, and that each gear moves freely on its shaft.
steps.title: Inspect the gearbox and shifting parts
verification: Forks, bars and shift drum good

steps.instruction: Measure each friction plate at four points: friction plates 1 spec 2.70–2.90 mm (limit 2.60 mm), friction plates 2 spec 2.72–2.88 mm (limit 2.62 mm). Check the steel plates for warpage on a surface plate (limit 0.10 mm). Measure each clutch spring free length (limit 42.28 mm; replace as a set). Roll push rod 2 for bend (limit 0.30 mm). Check the clutch housing dogs and boss splines for notching, the pressure plate for cracks, and the primary gears for wear or play.
steps.title: Measure the clutch

steps.instruction: Check the starter clutch rollers and the starter clutch gear contact face for wear. Fit the starter clutch gear onto the primary driven gear and hold the driven gear: turned clockwise it must lock, turned counterclockwise it must spin freely. Check the damper assembly and gears for burrs or wear.
steps.title: Check the starter clutch
verification: Starter clutch freewheels and locks correctly

steps.instruction: Check the pump housing, cover, rotors and drive shaft for cracks, scoring or wear. Assemble the rotors dry and turn the shaft; any roughness means a new pump assembly.
steps.title: Check the oil pump

steps.instruction: Grease the left case oil seal lip with lithium-soap grease and coat the crank journals with molybdenum disulfide grease. Using the crankshaft installer pot, bolt, M12 adapter and spacer, pull the crank into the left case bearing, keeping the rod held at the top of its stroke, until the crank seats against the bearing. Never hammer the crank in.
steps.title: Install the crankshaft

steps.instruction: Drop the balancer shaft in with its flat turned toward the crankshaft.
steps.title: Fit the balancer shaft

steps.instruction: Rebuild each shaft exactly as it came apart, with molybdenum disulfide oil on the gear bores and sliding gear faces, new circlips with their sharp edge away from the thrust washer and their ends on a spline crest, and a new greased O-ring on the drive axle. Fit the collar into the case oil seal with its slit toward the case. Fit the main axle and drive axle into the left case together. Oil the fork grooves and fit the forks: the left fork into the 5th wheel gear, the right fork into the 6th wheel gear, and the center fork into the 3rd/4th pinion gear. Fit the shift drum, then the long and short guide bars with their springs.
steps.title: Fit the gearbox

steps.instruction: Turn the shift drum by hand through every gear while turning the main axle; every gear must engage cleanly and the axles must spin freely in neutral.
steps.title: Check the shifting on the bench

steps.instruction: Press a new oil seal into the left case to an installed depth of 4.5–5.0 mm. Fit oil nozzle 1 to the right case (bolt 5 N·m (3.7 lb-ft), medium threadlocker). Fit the dowel pins, and spread a thin even bead of Yamaha bond No. 1215 on the left case joint face.
steps.title: Prepare the case halves
verification: Sealant even, not in oil passages

steps.instruction: Bring the rod up to the top of its stroke and lower the right case onto the left, tapping it down evenly with a soft hammer. Fit the bolts in their correct length positions and tighten them in a criss-cross in two stages to 12 N·m (8.9 lb-ft). Turn the crank and the main axle: both must turn freely.
steps.title: Close and torque the crankcases

steps.instruction: Fit the oil strainer (bolts 10 N·m (7.4 lb-ft)). Fit the timing chain, the exhaust-side chain guide and its stopper plate with medium threadlocker at 10 N·m (7.4 lb-ft).
steps.title: Fit the strainer, chain and guide
verification: Chain guide plate at 10 N·m (7.4 lb-ft)

steps.instruction: With the stopper lever pushed down, fit the segment so its projections sit in the slits of the shift drum, and tighten the segment bolt to 30 N·m (22 lb-ft) without jarring the stopper lever. Fit the stopper lever spring, collar and lever with threadlocker on its bolt at 10 N·m (7.4 lb-ft). Assemble the shift lever with its pawls, pins and springs (oiled), fit it with the shift guide and tighten the guide bolts with threadlocker to 10 N·m (7.4 lb-ft). Fit the shift shaft with its roller, spring and collar, oiled, and a new oil seal.
steps.title: Refit the shift mechanism

steps.instruction: Fit the relief valve spring, relief valve and pin before the primary drive gear and collar, and make sure the valve cannot fall out.
steps.title: Refit the relief valve

steps.instruction: Oil the drive shaft and rotors, fit the inner rotor with its dowel in the groove, the outer rotor and the cover (screw 6 N·m (4.4 lb-ft)). Fit the pump with threadlocker on its bolts at 5 N·m (3.7 lb-ft) and check it turns smoothly.
steps.title: Assemble and fit the oil pump

steps.instruction: Fit the collar and balancer weight gear with its lower spline lined up with the balancer shaft. Fit the balancer drive gear and collar with the punch marks of the two gears lined up and its lower spline lined up with the crank. Fit a new conical washer and the balancer weight gear nut at 50 N·m (37 lb-ft). Fit the primary drive gear, a new conical washer (convex side out) and the primary drive gear nut with threadlocker on the specified band of its thread at 105 N·m (77 lb-ft). Fit the balancer weight with its flat lined up with the shaft flat, a new conical washer and the balancer nut at 38 N·m (28 lb-ft). Keep the aluminum plate between the gears while torquing.
steps.title: Refit the balancer and primary drive
verification: Weight gear nut at 50 N·m (37 lb-ft)
Primary drive nut at 105 N·m (77 lb-ft)

steps.instruction: Rebuild the primary driven gear, absorbers and side plate with the 5XC-marked side of the absorbers toward the side plate and the B7B-marked side of the side plate toward the starter clutch, then fit the starter clutch with its arrow side toward the primary driven gear. Hold the housing with the sheave holder and fit the starter clutch screws with threadlocker at 12 N·m (8.9 lb-ft). Refit the damper assembly, collar and spacer.
steps.title: Rebuild the clutch housing and starter clutch
verification: Starter clutch screws at 12 N·m (8.9 lb-ft)

steps.instruction: Fit new dowels and gasket and the right crankcase cover, tightening the bolts in stages in a criss-cross to 10 N·m (7.4 lb-ft). Fit the push lever shaft with greased seal lips and oiled bearings.
steps.title: Refit the right case cover
verification: Right cover bolts at 10 N·m (7.4 lb-ft)

steps.instruction: Oil the primary driven gear bore and fit the primary driven gear, thrust washer and clutch boss and washer. Fit a new conical washer with its OUT mark facing away from the engine and a new boss nut with oiled thread and face; hold the boss with the clutch holder, torque the nut to 95 N·m (70 lb-ft) by hand (no impact wrench) and stake it into the main axle cutouts.
steps.title: Refit the clutch boss

steps.instruction: Oil every plate. Starting and ending with a friction plate, alternate friction and steel plates: one black-marked friction plate first, the six colored friction plates in the middle, and the second black-marked plate last.
steps.title: Refit the clutch plates
verification: Starts and ends with a black friction plate

steps.instruction: Fit the bearing, washer and a new circlip on push rod 1 and oil it. Fit push rod 2, the ball and push rod 1. Fit the pressure plate, lining its mark up with the punch mark on the clutch housing, then the six springs and bolts, tightened in stages in a criss-cross to 10 N·m (7.4 lb-ft).
steps.title: Refit the push rods, pressure plate and springs

steps.instruction: Fit a new clutch cover gasket and the cover, bolts in stages to 10 N·m (7.4 lb-ft). Fit a new oil filter element and cover with its O-ring (bolts 10 N·m (7.4 lb-ft)).
steps.title: Refit the clutch cover and oil filter

steps.instruction: Clean the crank taper and the rotor bore so they are dry. Fit the Woodruff key with its flat face parallel to the crank axis, slide the rotor on with its keyway over the key, fit the washer and nut, hold the rotor and torque the nut to 65 N·m (48 lb-ft).
steps.title: Refit the generator rotor
verification: Key flat parallel to the crank

steps.instruction: If the stator or crank position sensor was disturbed, refit them with threadlocker: stator screws 10 N·m (7.4 lb-ft), sensor bolts 10 N·m (7.4 lb-ft) and the lead holder (8 N·m (5.9 lb-ft), threadlocker), with sealant on the lead grommet.
steps.title: Check the stator and pickup in the cover
verification: Stator and sensor fasteners at spec

steps.instruction: Fit the dowels and a new gasket, then the left cover with its bolts in stages in a criss-cross to 10 N·m (7.4 lb-ft). Fit the shift pedal on its punch mark at 12 N·m (8.9 lb-ft).
steps.title: Refit the left case cover and shift pedal
verification: Left cover bolts at 10 N·m (7.4 lb-ft)

steps.instruction: Turn the crankshaft by hand through several turns (the piston is not fitted yet, so keep the rod clear of the case edge) and shift through every gear while turning the output shaft. Write down every part you replaced. Continue with the top end guide.
steps.title: Final bottom end check

title: Bottom end: split the cases and rebuild crank, gearbox, clutch, balancer and oil pump

completeness: Strips the generator, clutch, primary drive, balancer drive, starter clutch, oil pump and shift mechanism, splits the crankcases, removes the gearbox, balancer shaft and crankshaft, checks every wear limit, and rebuilds with new seals, gaskets and any worn parts back to a closed bottom end ready for the top end; crankshaft and connecting rod internal repair is not covered (the crank is replaced as an assembly).
critical_stop_conditions: Crankshaft runout over 0.030 mm or crank width outside 55.93–56.00 mm: replace the crankshaft assembly.
Main or drive axle runout over 0.08 mm/0.08 mm: replace the axle.
Crankcase cracked or a bearing bore loose: replace the crankcases.
Cases will not separate with light tapping: stop and look for a bolt you missed; never lever on the gasket faces.
Gearbox does not shift through every gear on the bench: open it again before fitting the top end.
Crankshaft will not turn freely after the cases are bolted: stop and find the cause.
entry_state: Engine out of the frame (engine removal guide) with the top end stripped to the crankcase: head, cylinder and piston removed (top end guide). Oil and coolant drained.
excluded: Connecting rod or crankshaft bearing replacement (crank assembly is replaced as a unit)
Gear-by-gear transmission rebuild beyond inspecting and replacing damaged gears
Water pump seal service
Starter motor overhaul

Fit a new conical washer with its OUT mark facing away from the engine and a new boss nut with oiled thread and face; hold the boss with the clutch holder, torque the nut to 95 N·m (70 lb-ft) by hand (no impact wrench) and stake it into the main axle cutouts.
steps.title: Refit the clutch boss

steps.instruction: Oil every plate. Starting and ending with a friction plate, alternate friction and steel plates: one black-marked friction plate first, the six colored friction plates in the middle, and the second black-marked plate last.
steps.title: Refit the clutch plates
verification: Starts and ends with a black friction plate

steps.instruction: Fit the bearing, washer and a new circlip on push rod 1 and oil it. Fit push rod 2, the ball and push rod 1. Fit the pressure plate, lining its mark up with the punch mark on the clutch housing, then the six springs and bolts, tightened in stages in a criss-cross to 10 N·m (7.4 lb-ft).
steps.title: Refit the push rods, pressure plate and springs

steps.instruction: Fit a new clutch cover gasket and the cover, bolts in stages to 10 N·m (7.4 lb-ft). Fit a new oil filter element and cover with its O-ring (bolts 10 N·m (7.4 lb-ft)).
steps.title: Refit the clutch cover and oil filter

steps.instruction: Clean the crank taper and the rotor bore so they are dry. Fit the Woodruff key with its flat face parallel to the crank axis, slide the rotor on with its keyway over the key, fit the washer and nut, hold the rotor and torque the nut to 65 N·m (48 lb-ft).
steps.title: Refit the generator rotor
verification: Key flat parallel to the crank

steps.instruction: If the stator or crank position sensor was disturbed, refit them with threadlocker: stator screws 10 N·m (7.4 lb-ft), sensor bolts 10 N·m (7.4 lb-ft) and the lead holder (8 N·m (5.9 lb-ft), threadlocker), with sealant on the lead grommet.
steps.title: Check the stator and pickup in the cover
verification: Stator and sensor fasteners at spec

steps.instruction: Fit the dowels and a new gasket, then the left cover with its bolts in stages in a criss-cross to 10 N·m (7.4 lb-ft). Fit the shift pedal on its punch mark at 12 N·m (8.9 lb-ft).
steps.title: Refit the left case cover and shift pedal
verification: Left cover bolts at 10 N·m (7.4 lb-ft)

steps.instruction: Turn the crankshaft by hand through several turns (the piston is not fitted yet, so keep the rod clear of the case edge) and shift through every gear while turning the output shaft. Write down every part you replaced. Continue with the top end guide.
steps.title: Final bottom end check

title: Bottom end: split the cases and rebuild crank, gearbox, clutch, balancer and oil pump
