steps.instruction: Make sure every hose, cable and loom is pulled clear of the engine bay so nothing gets trapped as the engine goes in.
steps.title: Check the frame side

steps.instruction: With a helper, lift the engine in from the right side, bottom first, and rest it on the jack so the mount holes line up roughly.
steps.title: Lift the engine in from the right
verification: Engine in the frame on the jack

steps.instruction: Grease the pivot shaft with molybdenum disulfide grease and push it through from the right side, pushing the dummy shaft out as it goes. Put lithium-soap grease on the nut threads and face and torque the pivot shaft nut to 85 N·m (63 lb-ft).
steps.title: Fit the pivot shaft
verification: Pivot shaft through from the right

steps.instruction: Fit the lower engine mounting bolt and torque it to 53 N·m (39 lb-ft). Fit the inside and outside lower brackets with their bolts at 34 N·m (25 lb-ft), then the front engine mounting bolt at 55 N·m (41 lb-ft).
steps.title: Fit the lower and front mounts

steps.instruction: Fit the right and left upper engine brackets with their bolts at 34 N·m (25 lb-ft) and the upper engine mounting bolt at 45 N·m (33 lb-ft). Remove the jack.
steps.title: Fit the upper brackets
verification: Upper bracket bolts at 34 N·m (25 lb-ft)

steps.instruction: Refit the brake pedal with its bolt at 26 N·m (19 lb-ft) and hook its spring back on. Push the cylinder head breather hose on. Leave the engine guard off until the oil is in.
steps.title: Refit brake pedal, breather and guard

steps.instruction: Push the radiator hoses fully onto the engine fittings and tighten the clamp screws to 1.5 N·m (1.1 lb-ft).
steps.title: Reconnect the radiator hoses

steps.instruction: Plug in the stator coil, crankshaft position sensor, coolant temperature sensor and gear position switch couplers, routing each lead back in its clips as in your photos. Refit the rectifier/regulator at 7 N·m (5.2 lb-ft) and the spark plug cap.
steps.title: Reconnect the electrics
verification: Wiring routed as in the photos

steps.instruction: Loop the chain over the drive sprocket, slide it onto the shaft, fit the lock washer and nut. With the bike in gear and the rear brake held, torque the nut to 75 N·m (55 lb-ft) and bend the lock washer up against a flat. Refit the chain guide on the case (4.0 N·m (3.0 lb-ft)). Refit the sprocket cover at 7 N·m (5.2 lb-ft).
steps.title: Refit the drive sprocket

steps.instruction: Slide the shift pedal on with its slit on the punch mark and tighten the bolt to 12 N·m (8.9 lb-ft).
steps.title: Refit the shift pedal

steps.instruction: Hook the cable onto the push lever, seat it in its holder and tighten the locknuts at the engine end to 7 N·m (5.2 lb-ft). Set the lever free play at the handlebar adjuster.
steps.title: Reconnect the clutch cable

steps.instruction: Remove the tape from the intake, fit the throttle body into the intake joint and the air filter case joint, and tighten the joint clamp screws to 3.0 N·m (2.2 lb-ft) (throttle body side) and 3.0 N·m (2.2 lb-ft) (air filter side). Plug in the injector and sensor couplers. Check the throttle snaps shut from full open.
steps.title: Refit the throttle body

steps.instruction: Fit new gaskets in the exhaust port, put the front head pipe on and run the nuts down evenly; tighten all the nuts to 7 N·m first, then to 10 N·m (7.4 lb-ft). Fit the rear pipe section and its clamp, and the pipe bracket bolt at 20 N·m (15 lb-ft).
steps.title: Refit the head pipe with new gaskets
verification: Head pipe nuts at 10 N·m (7.4 lb-ft)

steps.instruction: Slide the silencer on with a new gasket where one is fitted, fit its bolts at 30 N·m (22 lb-ft) (front) and 30 N·m (22 lb-ft) (rear), then tighten the exhaust clamps to 12 N·m (8.9 lb-ft), checking each joint is fully home and the clamps do not sit on the locating tabs.
steps.title: Refit the silencer

steps.instruction: Fit the crankcase oil drain bolt with a new gasket at 20 N·m (15 lb-ft). Fit the coolant drain bolt with a new copper washer at 10 N·m (7.4 lb-ft).
steps.title: Refit the drain bolts
verification: Coolant drain bolt at 10 N·m (7.4 lb-ft)

steps.instruction: Refit the engine guard with its bolts at 7 N·m (5.2 lb-ft).
steps.title: Refit the engine guard

steps.instruction: Fit the fuel tank (bolts 7 N·m (5.2 lb-ft)), reconnect the fuel hose connector until it clicks and the fuel pump coupler, and check the hose is not pinched.
steps.title: Refit the fuel tank

steps.instruction: Refit the shrouds (air scoops) (bolts 7 N·m (5.2 lb-ft)), side covers (7 N·m (5.2 lb-ft)) and seat (22 N·m (16 lb-ft)).
steps.title: Refit the bodywork

steps.instruction: Walk around the bike and check every connection against your photos. The engine still needs 0.95 L (1.00 US qt) of oil after a full rebuild and about 0.93 L (0.98 US qt) of coolant: go straight to the first-start guide before trying to run it.
steps.title: Ready for first start
verification: Oil and coolant still to fill

title: Put the engine back in the frame and reconnect everything

completeness: Fills oil and coolant after a rebuild, does the pre-start checks, starts and warms the engine, checks the oil and coolant levels the correct way for this engine, then runs the staged break-in with the checks between stages and the follow-up oil change and torque checks.
critical_stop_conditions: Oil pressure warning, knocking, rattling or a metallic noise: switch off immediately and investigate.
Coolant or oil leak at any joint: stop and fix before riding.
Engine overheats or coolant boils over: stop and find the cause.
Metal particles in the oil at the post-break-in change: strip and inspect the engine.
Starter spins but the engine does not turn: stop, this points to the starter clutch.
entry_state: Engine rebuilt and refitted, everything reconnected, oil and coolant empty.
excluded: Fuel-injection tuning or mapping
Carrying out the rebuild itself
exit_state: Engine filled, run in through both break-in stages, levels and fasteners checked, oil changed after break-in; ready to race or ride.
prerequisites: All rebuild guides completed and every fastener torqued.
Air filter cleaned and oiled before the first run.

required_parts.name: Engine oil 10W-40, 10W-50, 15W-40, 20W-40 or 20W-50, API service SG type or higher, JASO standard MA
required_parts.purpose: 0.95 L (1.00 US qt) for a rebuilt engine

required_parts.name: Ethylene glycol antifreeze for aluminum engines, mixed 1:1 with distilled water
required_parts.purpose: about 0.93 L (0.98 US qt)

required_parts.name: Oil filter element and O-rings
required_parts.purpose: New at the post-break-in oil change

required_parts.name: Fresh fuel
required_parts.purpose: Unleaded, as specified for the bike

required_tools.name: Tachometer function or the bike's own rpm reading if fitted

steps.instruction: With the bike upright on level ground, pour in 0.95 L (1.00 US qt) of 10W-40, 10W-50, 15W-40, 20W-40 or 20W-50 engine oil (API service SG type or higher, JASO standard MA). Do not use oil additives; the oil also runs the clutch. Refit the filler cap with its O-ring.
steps.title: Fill the engine oil
verification: Oil filled to the rebuild quantity

steps.instruction: Fill the radiator slowly with a 1:1 mix of ethylene glycol antifreeze (for aluminum engines) and distilled water, about 0.93 L (0.98 US qt). Squeeze the radiator hoses to push air out and top up until the level stays at the filler neck, then fit the radiator cap. Fill the reservoir, if fitted, to its full mark.
steps.title: Fill the coolant

steps.instruction: Fit a cleaned and oiled air filter. Check the throttle snaps shut, the clutch lever has free play or a firm hydraulic feel, all couplers are connected, there is fuel in the tank, and no tools or rags are left in the engine bay.
steps.title: Pre-start checks

steps.instruction: Put the gearbox in neutral and start the engine with the start button, using short attempts of no more than 10 seconds. Below about 15 °C (59 °F) air temperature, pull the starter knob all the way out before starting. Hold it at a steady 3000 to 5000 rpm for one or two minutes to warm up, then let it idle (stock idle is 1900–2100 r/min). Listen for any unusual noise.
steps.title: Start and warm up

steps.instruction: With the engine running, look around the head gasket, cylinder base, case covers, drain bolts, water pump and hose joints for oil or coolant. Switch off if you see a leak.
steps.title: Check for leaks

steps.instruction: Stand the bike upright, run the engine for 2 to 3 minutes, switch off and wait about a minute. The oil level must sit between the minimum and maximum marks in the check window. Top up if it is low.
steps.title: Check the oil level

steps.instruction: Let the engine cool completely. Then open the radiator cap slowly with a rag over it and top up to the neck; air worked its way out while the engine ran. Top up the reservoir too if fitted.
steps.title: Check the coolant level
verification: Coolant at the neck after cooling

steps.instruction: Ride for about 20 minutes using no more than half throttle. If you replaced the piston, rings, valves, camshafts or gears, this half-throttle running needs to total about 30 minutes; if you replaced the cylinder or the crankshaft, plan for about an hour of break-in in total. Vary the speed and avoid lugging or holding one rpm for long.
steps.title: Break-in stage 1: 20 minutes at half throttle
verification: About 20 minutes at half throttle or less completed

steps.instruction: Stop and check for loose fasteners, oil or coolant leaks, and anything that has moved.
steps.title: First pit stop

steps.instruction: Ride for about 40 minutes using no more than three-quarter throttle, still varying the load.
steps.title: Break-in stage 2: 40 minutes at three-quarter throttle
verification: About 40 minutes at three-quarter throttle or less completed

steps.instruction: Check everything thoroughly again: leaks, cable stretch, brake free play, chain slack and spoke tension. Recheck the torque on the engine mounts, pivot shaft, exhaust and other torque check points.
steps.title: Second check

steps.instruction: Drain the oil while warm and look for metal particles or debris; any found means the engine must be opened and checked. Replace the oil filter element and its O-rings and refill with 0.75 L (0.79 US qt) of oil. Recheck the level as before.
steps.title: Change the oil after break-in

steps.instruction: Check the generator rotor and stator mounting for looseness, the exhaust and silencer for cracks or leaks, and that no couplers have worked loose. The engine is now ready for normal use.
steps.title: Post-break-in engine checks

title: Fill, first start and break-in after an engine rebuild
